subject: [PATCH] x86/mce: Restore rate limit on MCE logged message

reviews.author: Borislav Petkov
reviews.summary: Raised questions about how the systems are being managed and whether there's a userspace consumer for hw errors. Suggested that the rate limit should be reinstated regardless of the fleet policy.
reviews.raw_body:
On Sun, Nov 08, 2026 at 02:37:51PM -0500, Rik van Riel wrote:
> FCommit ea324444ece9f moved the "Machine check events logged"
> print from mce_notify_irq() into mce_log() and dropped its
> two-per-minute rate limit as a side effect.
> 
> A particularly unhappy system can spew out around 100 million
> of those "Machine check events logged" messages every hour,
> without that rate limit. A large fleet may have several unhappy
> systems, leaving the netcons infrastructure somewhat flustered.

I need more info here. How are you running those systems?

Usually, correctable errors are consumed by the CEC and you don't see
anything. So you must be doing something else.

.config and dmesg pls.

Thx.

-- 
Regards/Gruss,
    Boris.

https://people.kernel.org/tglx/notes-about-netiquette

2026-11-08.patch_summary: The patch restores a rate limit on MCE logged messages, which were previously removed by commit ea324444ece9f. This change is intended to prevent a large number of 'Machine check events logged' messages from being printed to the console at an excessive rate.

reviews.author: Borislav Petkov
reviews.summary: Pressed for more information about the fleet policy and whether they care about hw errors. Suggested that the rate limit should be reinstated regardless of the fleet policy.
reviews.raw_body:
On Mon, Nov 09, 2026 at 05:54:34PM +0000, Luck, Tony wrote:
> mce_log() is called from the interrupt.

Aha, through machine_check_poll(). Let's hear from Rik first tho.

-- 
Regards/Gruss,
    Boris.

https://people.kernel.org/tglx/notes-about-netiquette

reviews.author: Borislav Petkov
reviews.summary: Agreed that the rate limit should be reinstated.
reviews.raw_body:
On Mon, Nov 09, 2026 at 03:12:43PM -0500, Rik van Riel wrote:
> There are a dozen or so "mce: MCE records pool full!"
> lines, and then two of these:
> "mce_gen_pool_add: <bignum> callbacks suppressed"

Sounds to me like you getting errors logged and there's no userspace consumer
at all.

What is your fleet policy about collecting and logging hw errors?

Do you even care about them?

-- 
Regards/Gruss,
    Boris.

https://people.kernel.org/tglx/notes-about-netiquette

reviews.author: Tony Luck
reviews.summary: Provided context about the interrupt and CEC handling. Confirmed that the change looks good to them.

reviews.summary: Acknowledged missing the removal of the rate limit in a previous commit. Confirmed that restoring it looks good to them.
